Cycad fronds lean directly over the lip, their undersides lime-gold in afternoon sun, casting barred shadow down the tunnel floor into the chamber.
Dense fern crowding the entrance, fronds bent inward, their tips trembling with the heat rising from the burrow, green light flooding the shaft.
Hot bleached plain beyond the mouth, grass white-gold at midday, heat shimmer bending the horizon line, fierce brightness spilling hard down the tunnel.
River running past the cut bank, surface a sheet of fractured silver, light bouncing off water strobing in quick flashes across the chamber ceiling.
Rain hammering the world above, water sheeting over the entrance lip in a thin continuous curtain, beading on exposed root-fibres just inside the mouth.
Deep forest floor dappled in slow-moving pools of gold, a single hard shaft of light falling directly onto the entrance, burning the rim white.
Dawn orange filling the opening completely, the mouth a perfect disc of amber, that warm colour reaching far down the tunnel floor in a long wedge.
Fern fronds pressing in from both sides, translucent green against strong backlight, their shadow-ribs lying in parallel across the packed earth just inside.
Sand trickling over the dune crest above, a thin thread of it spilling continuously over the entrance edge, piling in a small cone on the chamber floor.
Frost on every visible surface above, each grass blade rimed white, cold breath condensing in a pale cloud at the tunnel mouth where warm air meets outside.
Blossom petals drifting sideways past the opening on a lazy wind, two settling softly just inside the lip on the disturbed earth there.
A vast leg, column-grey and textured as bark, moving slowly past at a distance above, visible for a long moment through the bright tunnel mouth then gone.
River light, rippled and restless, reflected onto the underside of the overhang above the entrance, the whole burrow ceiling alive with moving water-brightness.
Cycad fronds arching directly across the mouth, their saw-edged shadows cutting the tunnel floor into alternating strips of amber and deep brown.
Heat plain shimmering beyond, the grass nearly white at the centre and deepening to tawny at the edges, the mouth framing it like a burning lens.
Snow lying above, the light from it even and blue-white, utterly unlike the amber of the chamber, the contrast fierce at the tunnel mouth.
Seed-fluff tumbling through the opening in a slow spiral, catching the last horizontal light of evening so each filament glows before settling on the floor.
Dusk filling the sky above the dune slope, the entrance a disc of deep apricot, sand still trickling over the lip in a steady fine stream.
Rain above, the drops catching low sunlight as they fall, each one a small spark, water collecting in a bright line along the lower rim of the mouth.
Deep forest beyond, nearly dark between the trunks, but one shaft of direct light striking the entrance from directly above, making the rim glow copper-gold.
Frost-rimed fronds hanging over the lip, their weight bowing them down into the opening, each edge silvered, cold light travelling the length of the tunnel.
Open plain blazing at midday, the grass a solid band of scorched gold across the lower half of the entrance circle, sky a hard cobalt above it.
Two enormous legs of a passing animal, dark against bright sky, crossing the tunnel mouth slowly from left to right, their shadow briefly dimming the chamber.
River bank above, the water audible, its reflected light rippling continuously across the root-threaded ceiling of the tunnel shaft close to the entrance.
Dense ferns backlit by an early sun so they blaze translucent yellow-green, three frond-tips curling down into the tunnel mouth, trembling with each outside gust.
